unite_adi: UPPER SECONDARY-YEAR 9 (AFTER PREP)-LEVEL: B2.1 - THEME 4: FAMILY LIFE & HOME

bolumler.ogrenmeKanitlari: PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT: Students will explore the theme ''Family Life and Home'' by examining ''housing diversity around the world'', ''intergenerational issues and family problems related to daily conflicts and sharing the same house'', and ''the relationships between families and their communities. Students will create a comparative project where they research different housing styles and living arrangements globally, reflecting on how culture and geography influence these differences. They will also write a short fictional story or script describing a typical day in a multi-generational household, highlighting challenges and solutions for improving harmony. The project will finish with the ways students will propose families to strengthen their ties with the community, such as through volunteering or cultural events. The assignment will be evaluated by using a rubric scheme, a rating scale, and/or a marking scheme. Öğrenme-Öğretme Yaşantıları
bolumler.temelKabuller: This theme includes the concept of ''family life and home with its components such as housing diversity in the world; intergenerational issues and family problems on daily conflicts and sharing the same house; relationships between the family and the community'' and it is assumed that it could be present in almost all languages, with some exceptions. It is assumed that a student in the after prep year 9 of an upper secondary school may know what housing diversity in the world; intergenerational issues and family problems on daily conflicts and sharing the same house; relationships between the family and the community mean in their as it is known that almost all people who start to learn a new language bring their pre-existing knowledge (in their own language) with them and transfer it to their new language learning context. However, they may not know how to say these things in a foreign language if this has not yet been covered in their existing curriculum. Fortunately, this existing knowledge in their own language can help them recognise, understand, and learn them more easily in a foreign language, in this case English. As they are students in the after prep year 9 of an upper secondary school, they are expected to know some basic vocabulary about ''family life and home'' and also some necessary structures in English from the previous themes and/or years. These grammar items and vocabulary are revised during the ''Revision Programme'' at the beginning of the year and they can be used as a basis for learning the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme, so that the new grammatical elements in the current theme can be learnt easily.
bolumler.onDegerlendirme: It is assumed that these students in the after prep year 9 of an upper secondary school are ready to learn the concept of ''family life and home with its components such as housing diversity in the world; intergenerational issues and family problems on daily conflicts and sharing the same house; relationships between the family and the community'' cognitively, affectively, and socially since it is appropriate to their age and language level. Therefore, a contextual poster or a large picture could be provided for the students to remember and practise the items that they are related and previously learnt so that they can discuss the poster and/ or the picture in pairs and write down what they remember. This session can help them revise all the related vocabulary and grammatical elements that they have already learnt from previous themes or from previous years as a preparatory practice. In this way, their performance can be evaluated in terms of how much they remember and how accurately they use these items to build their competence in the current theme. It can help the teacher decide what to emphasise, revise, and practise in order to facilitate the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme. (Their performance can be evaluated by rubrics, a rating scale, and /or a marking scheme during these practices.).
bolumler.zenginlestirme: Objective: To describe various types of homes and their features in English by using the target vocabulary. Activity 1: Exploring Homes Around the World Students work in groups of 3–4 to explore housing diversity by using target vocabulary and adjectives. Each group receives a list of housing types (e.g. a bungalow, a skyscraper, a mansion) and features (e.g. a chimney, a staircase, a terrace) along with a blank table labelled: Type of Home, Their Features, Adjectives to Describe It. Groups discuss and fill in the table by matching housing types with features and descriptive adjectives, then create sentences (e.g. ''A mansion is a spacious and luxurious home with an elegant staircase and a large chimney''). The teacher monitors discussions, provides feedback on the choice and use of vocabulary and pronunciation, and helps with accurate sentence formation. In the end, groups present their favourite housing type, by using sentences to describe it, and then the teacher gives constructive feedback. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
bolumler.destekleme: Objective: To describe personal family events in English by using target vocabulary and target grammar. Activity 1: Fill in the Blanks The teacher draws a simple timeline on the board and marks significant family events (e.g. moving to a new house, visiting relatives, celebrating birthdays), writes example sentences by using the Present Perfect Tense and Present Perfect Progressive Tense such as ''We have been living in this house for five years'' or ''My grandparents have visited us many times''. The teacher reads these sentences aloud by emphasising correct pronunciation and structure. Then students design their own timelines, mark 3–4 significant family events, and write sentences using provided sentences such as ''We have been ______ for ______ years'' or ''My family has ______ many times''. Finally, students take turns reading their sentences aloud while the teacher provides feedback on the language choice and use including target grammar, pronunciation, and accuracy. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
